translation_en: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim and Muhammad ibn Ja‘far ibn Ziyad narrated to us. Mansur said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from al-Zuhri; Ibn Ja‘far said: Ibrahim, Ibn Sa‘d, informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “A man used to lend to people and tell his servant, ‘When you come to someone in hardship, be lenient with him, perhaps Allah will be lenient with us.’ He met Allah, and Allah was lenient with him.”

Harmalah ibn Yahya informed us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah told him he heard Abu Hurayrah say he heard the Messenger of Allah say a report like it.

Abu al-Haytham Khalid ibn Khidash ibn ‘Ajlan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, that Abu Qatadah sought a debtor of his, who hid from him. When he found him, the man said, “I am in hardship.” He asked, “By Allah?” He replied, “By Allah.” Abu Qatadah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “Whoever wishes Allah to save him from the distresses of the Day of Resurrection, let him give respite to someone in hardship or remit his debt.”
Abu al-Tahir narrated it to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Ayyub, with this chain and a report like it.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “A wealthy person’s delay in repaying a debt is injustice. If one of you is referred to a solvent person, let him accept the referral.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: ‘Isa ibn Yunus informed us; Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us. Both said: Ma‘mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us: Waki‘ narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us. Both reported from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade selling surplus water.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah forbade selling the stud service of a camel, selling water, and selling land to be cultivated. The Prophet forbade these.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik; Qutaybah narrated to us: Layth narrated to us. Both reported from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Surplus water must not be withheld in order to prevent pasture from growing.”

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated it to me—and the wording is Harmalah’s. Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who told me that Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not withhold surplus water in order to prevent pasture from growing.”

Ahmad ibn ‘Uthman al-Nawfali narrated to us: Abu ‘Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Ziyad ibn Sa‘d informed me that Hilal ibn Usamah told him that Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed him he heard Abu Hurayrah say the Messenger of Allah said: “Surplus water must not be sold in order to sell pasture.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Mas‘ud al-Ansari, that the Messenger of Allah forbade the price of a dog, the earnings of a prostitute, and the fee given to a soothsayer.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn Rumh reported from al-Layth ibn Sa‘d; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us. Both reported from al-Zuhri with this chain and a report like it. Ibn Rumh’s version of al-Layth’s hadith says that he heard Abu Mas‘ud.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who said: I heard al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid narrating from Rafi‘ ibn Khadij: I heard the Prophet say: “The worst earnings are a prostitute’s fee, the price of a dog, and a cupper’s wages.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: al-Walid ibn Muslim informed us, from al-Awza‘i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: Ibrahim ibn Qariz narrated to me, from al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid: Rafi‘ ibn Khadij narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “The price of a dog is foul, a prostitute’s fee is foul, and a cupper’s earnings are foul.”
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with this chain and a report like it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to me, from al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid: Rafi‘ ibn Khadij narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah, with a report like it.

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A‘yan narrated to us: Ma‘qil narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, who said: I asked Jabir about the price of a dog and a cat. He said: The Prophet sternly forbade that.
Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ordered that dogs be killed.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ordered that dogs be killed and sent word to the districts of Madinah that they should be killed.

Humayd ibn Mas‘adah narrated to me: Bishr, Ibn al-Mufaddal, narrated to us: Isma‘il, Ibn Umayyah, narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah used to order that dogs be killed. We went out through Madinah and its outskirts and left no dog without killing it, to the point that we killed a small dog belonging to a Bedouin woman who had come with it.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ordered dogs to be killed except hunting dogs, sheepdogs, or livestock dogs. Ibn ‘Umar was told that Abu Hurayrah said “or a crop-protecting dog.” Ibn ‘Umar said, “Abu Hurayrah owns a crop.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Mansur informed me: Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah informed us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah ordered us to kill dogs, to the point that a woman would come from the desert with her dog and we would kill it. Then the Prophet forbade killing them and said: “You should kill the completely black dog with two spots, for it is a devil.”

‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who heard Mutarrif ibn ‘Abd Allah narrating from Ibn al-Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ordered that dogs be killed, then said: “What is the matter with them and dogs?” Then he granted an exemption for hunting dogs and sheepdogs.

Yahya ibn Habib narrated it to me: Khalid, Ibn al-Harith, narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: al-Nadr narrated to us; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us. All reported from Shu‘bah with this chain. Ibn Hatim’s report from Yahya adds that he granted permission for sheepdogs, hunting dogs, and crop-protecting dogs.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except a livestock dog or a trained hunting dog, loses two qirats from his deeds every day.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except a hunting dog or livestock dog, loses two qirats from his reward every day.”

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us. Yahya ibn Yahya said: Isma‘il, Ibn Ja‘far, informed us; the others said: he narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, who heard Ibn ‘Umar say the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except a trained hunting dog or livestock dog, loses two qirats from his deeds every day.”

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us. Yahya said he was informed; the others said: Isma‘il narrated to us, from Muhammad, Ibn Abi Harmalah, from Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except a livestock dog or hunting dog, loses one qirat from his deeds every day.” ‘Abd Allah said Abu Hurayrah added, “or a crop-protecting dog.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Waki‘ narrated to us: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Whoever keeps a fierce dog or a livestock dog loses two qirats from his deeds every day.” Salim said Abu Hurayrah used to add, “or a crop-protecting dog,” and he owned crops.
